recentItems.title: LGE 2026 | Service delivery issues affecting uMhlathuze Local Municipality
recentItems.description:
As South Africa heads towards the November Local Government Elections, political parties are stepping up their campaigns and engaging communities around issues that matter most to voters.

In uMhlathuze, in KwaZulu-Natal, the political conversation is gaining momentum. 

We spoke to representatives from different political parties to find out about their campaigns, their priorities, and what they believe needs to be done to address the issues facing communities.

recentItems.title: Motorists face record-high petrol and diesel prices this month
recentItems.description:
Motorists are bracing for sharp increases in fuel prices from Wednesday.

Both grades of petrol will rise by between R3,12 and R3,33 per litre, while diesel prices will increase by between R2,84 and R3,24 per litre.

The Department of Mineral and Petroleum Resources has confirmed the increases, which will push the price of petrol above R30 a litre for the first time.

recentItems.title: World Teachers' Day | Calls for greater protection, recognition and support for teachers
recentItems.description:
Today marks World Teachers' Day, highlighting the contribution of teachers and their vital role in shaping South Africa's future. This year's theme calls for greater protection, recognition and support for the teaching profession. 

But teacher unions say educators across the country continue to face overcrowded classrooms, safety concerns, difficult working conditions and ongoing disputes over salaries. 

Nomusa Cembi, SADTU National Spokesperson, Nkosiphendule Ntantala, NAPTOSA Deputy President and Sibusiso Malinga, President of the National Teachers Union - NATU, join in a discussion.

recentItems.title: Cutting Edge | Service delivery in the City of Johannesburg
recentItems.description:
As South Africa heads towards the local government elections, Cutting Edge takes a closer look at the state of service delivery in the City of Johannesburg — and asks whether the city’s financial resources are translating into the services residents need.

From informal settlements and townships to established suburbs, communities across Johannesburg are confronting many of the same challenges: unreliable water supplies, sewage flowing through streets, damaged infrastructure and long-standing maintenance problems. Residents say that even when problems are reported, their complaints often go unanswered.

Billions of rands are allocated to municipalities each year for infrastructure and basic services. Yet on the ground, there remains a visible gap between what is budgeted and what communities experience. Cutting Edge examines Johannesburg’s finances, its infrastructure and maintenance backlog, and the challenges facing the city as it tries to keep pace with growing demand.

Professor Zondi Mkhabela weighs in on the city’s finances and argues that integrated public-private partnerships may be needed to urgently tackle the infrastructure backlog. He also looks at the impact coalition politics can have on the ability of a city government to deliver services.

For residents, these are not simply questions of budgets and political structures. They are daily realities that affect access to water, sanitation, housing and basic dignity.

And with voter turnout already low in the previous local government elections, Cutting Edge asks whether growing frustration with service delivery could further influence residents’ willingness to participate in the upcoming polls.

recentItems.title: Motorists face record-high petrol and diesel prices this month
recentItems.description:
Motorists will face record-high petrol and diesel prices from Wednesday. 

Central Energy Fund data predicts an increase of around R3 a litre for both grades of petrol, and between R2,80 and R3,15 for diesel, seeing petrol cost more than R30 a litre. 

The Department of Minerals and Petroleum Resources will announce the official fuel price adjustments ahead of the increases on the 7th of October. 

The latest surge is largely due to higher international oil prices, together with escalating Middle East tensions and continued disruptions to crude supplies and shipping. 

Prof. Isaac Khambule, Political Economist from the University of Johannesburg , Jolanda Andrag Chief Operating Officer at AgriSA join us live.

recentItems.title: SIU on businessman Maumela's failed court bid
recentItems.description:
The High Court in Pretoria has dismissed an urgent bid by businessman Morgan Maumela and the MHR Maumela Family Trust to stop the sale of a Ferrari valued at no less than nine-point-five million rand. 

The luxury vehicle is among assets preserved by the Special Investigating Unit amid its probe into alleged corruption and maladministration at Thembisa Hospital, where about two-billion rand is alleged to have been looted. 

The court found that Maumela and the trust had failed to show a clear right to stop the sale or demonstrate that they would suffer irreparable harm if it went ahead. 

The SIU says the judgment affirms that preserved assets can be managed practically to protect their value, while the proceeds from the sale remain secured, pending the finalisation of the civil proceedings.
